issues.issue: Did the Trial Division have jurisdiction to stay the immigration inquiry, given the leave requirement in IRPA s.72(1)?
issues.applicant_position: Stay motion is interlocutory in the citizenship judicial review, so s.18.2 of the Federal Court Act applies.
issues.respondent_position: Trial Division lacks jurisdiction: a stay of an immigration matter needs leave under IRPA s.72(1).
issues.result_quote: I am prepared to assume without deciding that the Trial Division had jurisdiction under section 18.2 of the Federal Court Act

issues.issue: Does this Court have appellate jurisdiction to hear the appeal, given the certified question requirement?
issues.respondent_position: This Court lacks jurisdiction to hear the appeal.
issues.result_quote: Therefore, no certified question was required and this Court has the jurisdiction to hear the appeal.

issues.issue: Has the appellant shown an arguable case on the judicial review of the Governor in Council’s revocation order?
issues.applicant_position: Governor in Council misconstrued its s.10 Citizenship Act mandate and failed to give reasons.
issues.result_quote: these arguments meet the very low threshold for an arguable case in the context of a stay application

issues.issue: Would the appellant suffer irreparable harm if the immigration inquiry is not stayed?
issues.applicant_position: Inquiry stress and prospect of deportation cause irreparable harm.
issues.result_quote: that justifies the conclusion that the appellant failed to establish irreparable harm

issues.issue: Does the balance of convenience favour a stay of the immigration inquiry?
issues.result_quote: It is not necessary to consider the other arguments relating to irreparable harm, or the arguments relating to the balance of convenience.
